extracted.subtask_description: First-person mid-19th-century travel essay describing Parisian sights, institutions, and social customs with judgments about art, public buildings, and public policy. The text offers evaluative criteria for opera/ballet, exhibitions, palaces, railways, passports and other civic matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opera house physical and organizational qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: The house is very spacious, admirably planned, superbly fitted up, and every way adapted to its purpose; the charges moderate; the audience large and well dressed; the officers and attendants up to their business, and everything orderly and quiet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an index of a well-run national opera, look for spacious, well-planned accommodations, moderate prices, a respectable audience, attentive staff, and general orderliness and quiet. The author notes the French Government directly supports the Opera, implying institutional backing is a feature of a national cultural institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of spectacle and music in opera
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a drama of Action and of Spectacle, however, to which the Music is subordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate an opera by whether it is primarily a spectacle or a musical work; in this account the production prioritizes visual/action elements over musical excellence. The presence of hundreds of performers and lavish spectacle indicates a production where music plays a secondary role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral suitability of the opera for family/social life
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Opera is ever to become an element of Social life and enjoyment in New-York, I do trust that it may be such a one as thoughtful men may take their daughters to witness without apprehension or remorse. Its entire, palpable, urgent tendency, is 'earthly, sensual, devilish.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A social-cultural standard: an opera fit for family attendance should not weaken instincts of purity or promote sensuality. Productions that tend toward eroticism or moral degradation are judged unfit for respectable social life; anti-patterns include spectacles that cultivate lax attitudes toward marriage and purity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballet as wholesome dance versus spectacle/exploitative display
rubrics_metrics.description: France is the cradle and home of the Ballet... 'poetry of motion'... natural expressions of innocent gaiety and youthful elasticity of spirits. But the more extravagant distortions... seem devised only to favor a liberal display of the person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ballet's ideal is graceful, healthful dance promoting beauty and vigor; it should be restricted to proper hours and fit associates. Extravagant feats that emphasize contortions or promote indecent display are disfavored. Evaluate dancers and choreography for grace, healthful expression, and avoidance of lasciviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of young performers / age-appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: The dancing-girls engaged were... apparently all between fourteen and eighteen years of age, generally good-looking, and with that aspect of innocence and freshness to which the Stage is so fatal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess productions for the use and protection of young performers; employing very young dancers in large spectacles is framed as potentially harmful and exploitative. Watch for claqueurs and hired applause that encourage improper displays; prefer settings where young performers are not exposed to corrupting influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function and purpose of international exhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the Exhibition is not merely to set forth what is best but to compare it with the inferior, and so indicate the readiest mode of improving the latter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exhibition should include a wide range of national products (both excellent and imperfect) so visitors can learn and improvements be identified. Criticism prior to juried evaluation is an anti-pattern: the press should not forestall the competent jurors' impartial verdicts. Trust the appointed juries to render fair assessment after inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and competence of juries at exhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Jurors appointed to judge and report upon the merits of rival fabrics were making the requisite investigations... They are competent; they have made the requisite examinations; they (though nearly all European and a majority of them British) are honorable men, and will render an impartial judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating exhibits, give weight to formal juries who have inspected items; avoid trusting premature press judgments. The credibility of awards rests on jurors' competence and honesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public galleries and monuments should avoid glorifying war
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideas everywhere predominant are War and its misnamed Glory... The whole collection is, in its general effect, delusive and mischievous, the purpose being to exhibit War as always glorious and France as uniformly triumphant... a full half of the story... is utterly suppressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate public art and palace galleries for balance and historic honesty. Paintings and displays that emphasize victories while suppressing defeats promote a dangerous, misleading martial glorification and can inflame youth toward war. Prefer balanced, historically truthful representation over triumphalist propaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repurposing grand royal palaces for public utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Some of them may be converted into Hospitals, Insane Retreats, &c., others into Libraries or Galleries of Art and Science... Perhaps it will be best... to convert all the others into direct uses and preserve [Versailles] for public inspection as a perpetual memorial...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large, costly former royal residences are appropriate targets for conversion to public uses (hospitals, asylums, libraries, galleries). Consider keeping at least one as a museum or memorial of monarchical excess while reutilizing others for social benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public cost and moral critique of royal expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: Versailles alone cost some Thirty Millions of Dollars at first... France... has paid more as simple interest on the residences of her monarchs... than the United States... pays for the entire cost of the Legislative, Executive and Judicial departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess royal or state spending on palaces by comparing social cost versus public benefit. Lavish expenditures that serve monarchs' pomp at the expense of the populace are judged reckless and politically injurious; fiscal accountability and redirection to public uses are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Railway passenger accommodations and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Railway carriages, so far as I have yet seen them, are more expensive and less convenient than ours. Each is absolutely divided into apartments... calculated to hold eight persons... thirty-two seats where an American car of equal length and weight would hold at least fifty, and of the thirty-two passengers, one-half must inevitably ride backward. ... baggage must be weighed and extra fees charged; strict first-class exclusion of companions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate train design by seating capacity, passenger convenience, ability to travel facing forward, reasonable baggage allowances and fees, and social accessibility between companions. Class-segregated entry that prevents companions from accompanying travelers and burdensome baggage charges are cited as negative features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passport and traveler formalities should not be oppressive
rubrics_metrics.description: If each American could spend three days on this continent, his love of Country and of Liberty could not fail to be quickened and intensified, if only by an experience of the enormity of the Passport nuisance. It has cost me precious hours already, not to speak of dollars... It is a shame that Republican France stands far behind Aristocratic Britain in this respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel document regimes should be reasonable and not impose excessive time or cost burdens on travelers. Overly pedantic enforcement (e.g., landlords refusing guests for passport phrasing, requiring odd profession translations) is an anti-pattern that discourages travel and reflects poor policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visiting major religious monuments (Notre Dame) as essential
rubrics_metrics.description: I attended divine worship to-day at Notre Dame, which seems to me not only the finest Church but the most imposing edifice in Paris... I trust no American visits Paris without seeing this noble church, and on the Sabbath if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cultural travelers, certain religious monuments are essential visits; to fully appreciate such buildings, attend liturgical services (Sabbath) when possible. The author recommends Notre Dame as a superior example, comparing it favorably to Westminster Abbey.
